article.title: Riverton council votes to cut downtown speed limit to 30 km/h
article.author: Staff reporter
article.text:
Riverton will lower the speed limit on downtown residential streets to 30 km/h starting in March, after council voted 7–4 on Tuesday.

Councillor Dana Ito, who backed the change, said slower streets save lives. “A pedestrian hit at 30 km/h usually survives. At 50, most do not,” she said, citing a transportation safety report presented to council.

Opponents said the rule will be hard to enforce. Councillor Rob Mercer noted the city has only four traffic officers for the entire downtown core. “A sign is not a speed bump,” he said.

City staff said signage will cost about $310,000, and that the city plans to add raised crosswalks on six streets next year.
